title: Quarterly Compatibility Corridor & Ops Handshake — Private/VPC Roadmap
creator: Priya Nair
body:
Objective: Define a repeatable 'Compatibility Corridor' — a set of deterministic gating signals and milestone threads that coordinate Platform, Runtime, Infra, Console, and Solutions teams for quarterly private/VPC/on-prem feature releases. The corridor reduces late surprises by aligning compatibility checks, customer-facing activation policies, and fallback/rollback choreography.

Scope:
- Establish mandatory pre-merge compatibility gates (integration test matrix, agent upgrade checks, KMS/HSM smoke tests).
- Define a cross-team 'ops handshake' protocol for cutover windows including preflight checklist, canary cohort sizing, and automated rollback triggers.
- Produce a compact runbook template and a visibility dashboard slice in Console for each release wave showing readiness signals.
- Pilot corridor on two upcoming customer activations (large regulated SaaS customer + mid-market cohort).

Success criteria / Acceptance:
- Each release has all corridor gates recorded with green/yellow/red signals in Console 96 hours before window.
- Canary cohort deployment triggers automatic scaling and owner-notifications on SLA regressions (>5% error rate or 2x latency baseline).
- Zero customer-facing incidents requiring emergency rollback in pilot tenants during the pilot window.
- Post-release survey from Solutions & Customer Success scores the ops handshake as 'sufficient' or better for >=80% of activations.

Milestones & timeline:
- Week 1: Finalize gate definitions and owner mappings (Platform, Runtime, Infra, Console, Sec)
- Week 2: Implement Console dashboard slice + ingestion of gating signals
- Week 3: Write runbook templates and automation for canary cohort sizing
- Week 4: Dry-run with internal 'shadow' tenant and incorporate feedback
- Week 6-8: Pilot with 2 external customers; collect telemetry and incident learnings
- Week 9: Post-mortem and roadmap handoff for scaling corridor across all private waves

Key stakeholders:
- PM: Priya Nair
- Eng leads: Diego Morales (Platform), Mei Zhang (Runtime), Arjun Patel (Infra)
- Design: Lina Gomez (Console UX)
- Solutions/CS: Marcus Reed
- Security: Elena Ivanova

Trade-offs considered:
- Strict pre-merge gates increase velocity friction; mitigated by automated preflight and parallel staging.
- Larger canary cohorts reduce false positives but increase blast radius; default to conservative 5% cohort with policy override for critical customers.

Open questions:
- What is the minimal test matrix that prevents the most common regressions without excessive runtime cost?
- Which metrics should trigger automatic rollback vs. manual intervention? Proposal: automatic on safety/security signals; manual for quality regressions unless they exceed severe thresholds.

Links:
- Draft spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/private-compatibility-corridor
- Pilot checklist doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/private-pilot-checklists
- Related Linear tickets: ENG-62198 (KV cache stability), ENG-63420 (KMS integration)

Next steps:
- Lock gate owners and publish the corridor spec to stakeholders (due in 3 business days)
- Kick off Console dashboard spike with Lina to finalize telemetry contract
